title: Stop or continue an enclosing loop directly
goal: Use labeled break and continue in C# 15 when a nested traversal must stop an enclosing loop or skip its remaining work while preserving cleanup.

runtime.reason: This documented application route targets net11.0; labeled jumps do not introduce a separate library dependency.
runtime.name: .NET

sdk.reason: Use the .NET 11 SDK family providing C# 15 and the target reference assemblies.
sdk.name: .NET SDK

language.reason: Labeled break and continue are C# 15 syntax, stabilized in the canonical RC1 notes.
language.name: C#

prerequisites: Target net11.0 with LangVersion 15.0, implicit usings enabled and nullable enabled.
constraints: The label must immediately mark an enclosing target; continue can target only a loop.
A jump cannot cross a function boundary or leave a finally block; cleanup runs for scopes actually exited.
No supported C# 15 route for an older target is claimed.
stabilityLimitations: Verified using .NET 11 RC2 artifacts only; GA reconciliation is pending.

selectionNotes: Targets an enclosing labeled construct; continue requires a loop. Function and finally boundaries still apply.
No supported older-target C# 15 route is claimed.

sources.title: Microsoft statement specification and cleanup semantics

evidence.scope: Actual builds and executions of identical checks for batch skipping, early termination, ordinary/empty traversal and ordered finally/using cleanup. No mocks or cross-compilation; exact commands, inputs and output are retained in the saved records.
